messages.subject: warping along PC2
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I am trying to use the 'plotTangentSpace' command to warp a mesh along principle component axes, which I have done successfully along PC1. However, when I try to use it to warp the mesh along PC2, it appears that the negative and positive warps are identical. This has occurred for multiple datasets, and also when I use the command 'plotRefToTarget'.

Below is the code I used for warping along PC2 with 'plotTangentSpace':

plotTangentSpace(A, axis1 = 2, axis2 = 3, warpgrids = TRUE, mesh = ply)

And here is the code I used with 'plotRefToTarget':

ref_j <- mshape(A) #get mean of lmrk coords
plotRefToTarget(ref_j, PCA$pc.shapes$PC2min, mesh = ply, method = "surface")  #PC2min
plotRefToTarget(ref_j, PCA$pc.shapes$PC2max, mesh = ply, method = "surface")  #PC2max

Am I doing something wrong? I used both commands on two different datasets and negative and positive warps still looked identical. However, when I use either command to warp along PC1, there are very clear differences.

Thanks for any help,

Sakib

Dear Sakib,

Assuming you have the most recent install of geomorph, You only need to run plotTangentSpace once to get all of the shapes returned under PCA$pc.shapes (providing you are executing
PCA <- plotTangentSpace()

How much of the shape variation is described by PC2? Look at the summary output from plotTangentSpace. It may be that the shape variation is small and you need to magnify the shape changes using the "mag" option in plotRefToTarget

Emma

messages.subject: 2B-PLS question
messages.body_plain:
Hi geomorphers!

I am interested in using integration methods such as 2B-PLS on shape data from 4 different taxa with intraspecific variation. I was able to successfully run 2B-PLS in geomorph considering all data points as independent. However, I am wondering if there is a way to consider the group structure in the analysis. In other words, I was able to produce a best fit line by simply plotting my 2B-PLS results, but is there a way to consider that my taxonomic groups might be following different patterns of integration? Any help would be greatly appreciated!

Best,
Angie Peña

messages.subject: Basic ANOVA and discriminant functions
messages.body_plain:
Pardon the basic questions...

1.My first question is probably highly ignorant, but as a non-power user I've been stuck since the change happened. What's the easiest way to replicate the old (but inaccurate), simple pairwise comparisons that procD.lm would produce in the case of (coords~groups)? I understand that advanced.procD.lm can do it with complex models, but I can't figure out how to get the easy stuff out.

2. Is there a convenient way or some available code to do discriminant analysis in geomorph, again in a (coords~groups) setup? Apparently there's a way to do it using the mass::lda package, but trying to keep it simple for my students.

Thanks.

-Russ

messages.body_plain:
Russ,

Use advanced.procD.lm and have as models and group crierion:

coords ~ group, coords ~1, groups = ~group

The latter means the model only contains an intercept, which is the overall mean.  Thus, you are comparing a group means model to a single mean model.  That will perform the same multiple comparisons test as old.

Mike

Russ,

We do not supply discriminant analysis through geomorph, but as you stated the lda() function is readily available in the mass package in R.  If one wishes to perform such an analysis, simply take your shape variables and convert them to a matrix:

myshape<-two.d.array(GPA-aligned coords)

This creates a matrix of rows = specimens and cols = variables. Use this as input in lda.

Dean

messages.subject: GMM LDA
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

So i have a dataset of 688 faces and a binary grouping variable (let's call it 2 types of photo) and want to run LDA on it. I have 53 landmarks so my procrustes aligned dataset is a 53x2x688 matrix. As they are faces they have been aligned assuming object symmetry, so i think the "shape" variable in the geomorph dataframe reflects the symmetrical component of variation.

I heard that i need to convert it to a 688x106 matrix using two.d.array, but when i do that and run the LDA i get :

"Error in lda.default(x, grouping, ...) :  variables  38  72  78  92 102 appear to be constant within groups"

This presumably means that these variables have no variance within the groups on these landmarks. However when i remove these variables it just says the different ones are constant, and it finds a new one whenever i remove one!

Does anyone know what's going on here? i've been at this for like a day now.

Cheers,

Richie

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] GMM LDA
messages.body_plain:
Hi Richie,

I would use plotTangentSpace on your shape variables instead of two.d.array.  If you do not mess with the default arguments, the $pc.scores object created will shave off the extra dimensions.  If you do this and still have trouble (you shouldn’t), you can always remove the last column or two of the matrix, as the principal components will have the most variation among specimens represented in the earliest dimensions.

I was not aware that lda.defult had such a trap.  It would not be an issue for classification, but maybe it’s there to prevent strange discriminant functions.  Hopefully using PC scores will not disrupt your intended use of discriminant analysis.

Cheers!
Mike

If you do this and still have trouble (you shouldn’t), you can always remove the last column or two of the matrix, as the principal components will have the most variation among specimens represented in the earliest dimensions.
>
> I was not aware that lda.defult had such a trap.  It would not be an issue for classification, but maybe it’s there to prevent strange discriminant functions.  Hopefully using PC scores will not disrupt your intended use of discriminant analysis.
>
> Cheers!
